recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一顆嗜中性球的核完全沒有分葉，呈單一圓到卵圓形、染色質粗塊濃縮，但細胞質已有成熟的淡粉紅顆粒，核質成熟度不相符（非分葉的成熟嗜中性球），是 Pelger-Huët 變異型。
features: Neutrophil-sized cell with a single round to oval, non-lobated nucleus
Coarse, clumped mature chromatin despite lack of segmentation
Abundant pale cytoplasm with fine neutrophilic granules and a few small vacuoles
Normal granulation without hypogranularity in this cell
Background red cells with rouleaux-like overlap and scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a mature neutrophil with a single round to oval, non-lobated nucleus containing coarse, clumped mature chromatin. The cytoplasm is abundant and pale with fine neutrophilic granules and a few small vacuoles. The combination of fully mature chromatin with absence of lobation distinguishes this cell from a myelocyte. The appearance represents a non-segmented Pelger-Huët-type neutrophil; the inherited anomaly is diagnosed when most neutrophils are hyposegmented with normal granulation, while an acquired pseudo-Pelger-Huët change should raise concern for myelodysplasia or drug effect.

ddx.vs: Myelocytes have finer, less condensed chromatin and often a paler Golgi zone, while this cell has fully clumped mature chromatin.

Morphology of a single cell is similar; acquired forms show hypogranularity, other dysplastic lineages and involve only a subset of neutrophils, whereas the inherited anomaly affects nearly all neutrophils uniformly.
Monocytes have folded nuclei with lacy chromatin and gray-blue cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granules, not coarse condensed chromatin.
Lymphocytes have scant basophilic cytoplasm without neutrophilic granules.
